construct: Hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia is an autosomal dominant vascular dysplasia most commonly caused by pathogenic variants in ENG or ACVRL1, genes in TGF-beta/BMP signaling pathways. Patients form mucocutaneous telangiectases and arteriovenous malformations that lack an intervening capillary bed.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Recurrent spontaneous epistaxis, mucocutaneous telangiectases, visceral AVM in a first-degree relative, and an autosomal-dominant pattern identify hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Ataxia-telangiectasia includes telangiectases, but it presents in childhood with progressive cerebellar ataxia and immunodeficiency and does not produce this familial epistaxis/visceral-AVM phenotype.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The Curacao-type clinical pattern makes HHT the only option that accounts for all findings.
